title: The Fear of Man Brings a Snare
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: Defining the Fear of Man
subpoints: It is a moral fear, distinct from physical danger.
It acts as a controlling force that overrides allegiance to God.
It prevents doing what is right or encourages doing what is wrong.

outline.title: Biblical Examples of Fearing Man
subpoints: Abraham and Isaac lied to protect their lives (Genesis 12).
Secret disciples in John 12 loved human praise more than God's.
The servant in the Parable of the Talents buried his gift out of fear.

outline.title: Manifestations and Roots of the Fear
subpoints: Includes people-pleasing, pride, perfectionism, and anxiety.
Can hinder evangelism, doctrinal integrity, and marital unity.

outline.title: The Danger of the Snare
subpoints: The fear of man is a hidden trap that leads to spiritual destruction.
It is incompatible with the fear of God (serving two masters).
It contradicts the biblical order of loving God before loving others.

summary:
This sermon examines the concept of the 'fear of man' as presented in Proverbs 29:25, defining it not as a physical safety concern but as a moral fear that controls behavior and compromises allegiance to God. The teaching distinguishes this spiritual snare from legitimate caution, emphasizing that it often manifests as people-pleasing, pride, perfectionism, or anxiety. By analyzing biblical examples such as Abraham, Isaac, and the secret disciples in John 12, the message illustrates how even faithful individuals can fall into the trap of prioritizing human approval over divine command.

The sermon identifies the root of this fear as idolatry and self-worship, arguing that it is a destructive sin that prevents believers from loving God properly and, consequently, from loving others effectively. It contrasts the pop-psychology view of self-love with the biblical mandate to love God first, noting that fearing man is an attempt to serve two masters, which Jesus declares impossible. The fear of man is described as a hidden snare that can lead to spiritual ruin if not addressed.

The call to action is to repent of this fear and embrace the fear of God, trusting in the Lord for safety rather than seeking security in human opinion. The sermon encourages believers to recognize the subtle ways this fear operates in daily life, from social media presentation to evangelism and marital relationships, and to rely on the truth that only the fear of God leads to true freedom and salvation.
